paper_title: Seeking dark matter with gamma-ray attenuation
notes: ALP dark-matter decay (a -> gamma gamma) contribution to extragalactic gamma-ray optical depth (EBL). Curve is the 'This work' upper bound in the bottom panel of Fig. 3 (g_agamma vs m_a c^2), extracted from the vector file constraints_zoom_3sigma.pdf: the top edge of the outermost dark-blue confidence contour (thick solid line at low mass, dashed at m>~18 eV where neutral-hydrogen absorption affects the analysis). Paper shows nested 68/95/99% contours; the emphasized outer boundary reported here is the 99% CL, which the paper/abstract/conclusions call the 'strongest 3-sigma bound' over the 8-25 eV mass range. Coupling convention matches the canonical L=-(g_agamma/4) a F Ftilde: verified via Gamma_a = (m_a c^2)^3 g_agamma^2/(64 pi) reproducing the paper's quoted best fit g_agamma=2.1e-11 GeV^-1 at m=9.1 eV for Gamma_a=2.5e-24 s^-1 (no conversion needed). No local halo density is assumed (extragalactic decay; ALPs taken as 100% of the cosmological dark matter, Omega_a=Omega_DM); the compilation does not rescale. The full 'This work' curve spans ~0.9-44 eV; it is the strongest bound only over ~8-25 eV. Small gaps in x-sampling (~3.4-5.5 eV, ~14.6-22.5 eV) are where the vector stroke path was interrupted; the underlying boundary is smooth and monotonic.
